questions.topic: Immunization, Infection Control, and Isolation Precautions
questions.stemEn: A NICU had five MRSA cases in a short period. What is the most likely cause of the outbreak?
questions.explanationAr: انتقال MRSA داخل NICU غالبًا يرتبط بـhand transmission أو colonized healthcare workers مع ضعف الالتزام بإجراءات infection control. لذلك مفتاح المصدر هو poor infection control compliance.
questions.reasoningEn: Healthcare-worker hand transmission and colonization are well-described drivers of NICU MRSA spread.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Poor medical management وantibiotic misuse قد يساهمان في resistance أو outcomes، لكنهما ليسا التفسير المباشر الأكثر شيوعًا لcluster قصير المدى.
questions.clinicalPearl: In an outbreak, think transmission chain first: hand hygiene, contact precautions, cohorting and colonization control.

tts.text: A NICU had five MRSA cases in a short period. What is the most likely cause of the outbreak? A. Poor infection control compliance. B. Poor medical management. C. Antibiotic misuse.

questions.topic: Immunization, Infection Control, and Isolation Precautions
questions.stemEn: A preterm infant in intensive care suddenly deteriorates. Blood cultures from both central and peripheral lines grow coagulase-negative Staphylococcus. What is the management?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار vancomycin ويذكر أن الخطة المثالية تشمل repeat blood culture، مع التفكير بإزالة central line إذا كان الطفل unstable أو بقيت cultures positive. السؤال مختصر لذلك لا نختزل management إلى دواء واحد قبل المراجعة.
questions.reasoningEn: Vancomycin provides empiric coverage for methicillin-resistant coagulase-negative staphylococci, but line management and repeat cultures depend on clinical context.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Cefotaxime لا يغطي methicillin-resistant CoNS بشكل موثوق. Repeat culture مهم لكنه ليس وحده علاجًا. Line removal يعتمد على instability أو persistent bacteremia.
questions.clinicalPearl: For catheter-related bloodstream infection, organism, clinical stability, persistent bacteremia and line necessity all matter.

tts.text: A preterm infant in intensive care suddenly deteriorates. Blood cultures from both central and peripheral lines grow coagulase-negative Staphylococcus. What is the management? A. Start cefotaxime. B. Start vancomycin. C. Repeat another blood culture. D. Remove central line.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection 4th Ed 2026
sourceRefs.notes: Source also references PREP 2024 Q129 and states vancomycin plus repeat culture; line removal is context-dependent.

verification.referenceNotes: Incomplete recall; verify neonatal CLABSI management before publication.

questions.topic: Immunization, Infection Control, and Isolation Precautions
questions.subtopic: Breastfeeding precautions with maternal genital lesions
questions.stemEn: A mother with genital warts delivered a term baby by cesarean section. What precaution should she follow during breastfeeding?
questions.explanationAr: مفتاح المصدر هو hand washing، لكن الشرح المرفق يتحدث عن active herpes lesions وليس HPV genital warts. هذا mismatch واضح بين stem والشرح، لذلك لا نعتمد verifiedAnswer الآن.
questions.reasoningEn: Basic hand hygiene is reasonable, but the source explanation does not match the stated diagnosis of genital warts.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: لا يمكن الحكم النهائي على بقية الخيارات لأن مصدر الشرح نفسه غير متطابق مع stem.
questions.clinicalPearl: When the stem and explanation describe different infections, preserve the recall but block publication pending verification.

tts.text: A mother with genital warts delivered a term baby by cesarean section. What precaution should she follow during breastfeeding? A. Wash hands. B. Nothing. C. Soap and water.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection 4th Ed 2026
sourceRefs.notes: Also 2017. Source explanation discusses herpes rather than HPV genital warts.

questions.topic: Immunization, Infection Control, and Isolation Precautions
questions.stemEn: An infant has a pertussis picture with cough and post-tussive vomiting. What is the proper isolation?

options.text: Droplet isolation until 5 days on treatment
Contact isolation after 24 hours from starting antibiotics

questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار Droplet precautions حتى إكمال 5 أيام من effective antibiotic therapy. لأن infection-control recommendations قابلة للتحديث، يبقى التحقق النهائي مطلوبًا.
questions.reasoningEn: Pertussis is transmitted by respiratory droplets; the source uses five days of effective therapy as the discontinuation threshold.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Contact isolation وحده لا يطابق طريقة الانتقال الأساسية للـpertussis.
questions.clinicalPearl: Isolation duration questions are guideline-sensitive: preserve the exam key and freshness-check before publishing.

tts.text: An infant has a pertussis picture with cough and post-tussive vomiting. What is the proper isolation? A. Droplet isolation until five days on treatment. B. Contact isolation after twenty-four hours from starting antibiotics.

questions.topic: Immunization, Infection Control, and Isolation Precautions
questions.stemEn: The mother of a child with positive streptococcal pharyngitis asks when the child can return to school. What do you advise?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار العودة بعد 24 ساعة من بدء العلاج. هذه نقطة guideline-sensitive وقد تختلف الصياغة الحديثة حسب كون الطفل afebrile وتحسن الأعراض ومدة العلاج الفعال، لذلك نثبت recall ولا ننشرها كقاعدة حديثة قبل التحقق.
questions.reasoningEn: The recalled exam key uses 24 hours of therapy as the threshold for school return.
questions.clinicalPearl: Return-to-school criteria should be checked against current public-health guidance.

tts.text: The mother of a child with positive streptococcal pharyngitis asks when the child can return to school. A. After twenty-four hours on treatment.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection 4th Ed 2026

questions.topic: Immunization, Infection Control, and Isolation Precautions
questions.stemEn: When should isolation be discontinued for Neisseria meningitidis infection?

options.text: After 24 hours of starting effective antibiotics
After 48 hours of starting effective antibiotics

questions.explanationAr: المصدر يذكر استمرار Droplet precautions لمدة 24 ساعة بعد بدء effective antibiotics، ثم يمكن إيقافها.
questions.reasoningEn: The source states that viable meningococci are no longer isolated after 24 hours of effective antimicrobial therapy.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: 48 ساعة أطول من threshold المذكور في المصدر.
questions.clinicalPearl: Close contacts still require chemoprophylaxis when indicated; stopping patient isolation does not replace contact management.

tts.text: When should isolation be discontinued for Neisseria meningitidis infection? A. After twenty-four hours of starting effective antibiotics. B. After forty-eight hours of starting effective antibiotics.

questions.topic: Immunization, Infection Control, and Isolation Precautions
questions.stemEn: A girl had fever for three days and then developed a slapped-cheek rash after the fever resolved. When can she return to school?
questions.explanationAr: في erythema infectiosum، ظهور slapped-cheek rash يحدث عادة بعد مرحلة viremia الأعلى عدوى؛ لذلك المصدر يقول إن exclusion من school بعد ظهور rash غير ضروري.
questions.reasoningEn: Parvovirus B19 infectivity is greatest before the characteristic rash appears.
questions.clinicalPearl: The rash is a late immune-mediated manifestation; infectiousness is usually highest earlier.

image.captionEn: Original source image shows the slapped-cheek rash.

tts.text: A girl had fever for three days and then developed a slapped-cheek rash after the fever resolved. When can she return to school? A. She can return now.

questions.topic: Immunization, Infection Control, and Isolation Precautions
questions.stemEn: What is the proper isolation for a suspected case of measles?
questions.explanationAr: Measles شديد العدوى وينتقل عبر airborne route، لذلك مفتاح المصدر هو Airborne isolation.
questions.reasoningEn: Measles requires airborne precautions because infectious particles can remain suspended in air.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Droplet أوContact وحدهما غير كافيين حسب مفتاح المصدر.
questions.clinicalPearl: Suspected measles should trigger prompt airborne precautions and public-health notification according to local policy.

tts.text: What is the proper isolation for a suspected case of measles? A. Airborne isolation. B. Droplet isolation. C. Contact isolation.

questions.topic: Immunization, Infection Control, and Isolation Precautions
questions.stemEn: A 7-year-old unvaccinated child with asthma has been receiving methylprednisolone 2 mg/kg/day for seven days. He had contact with a measles case two days ago. What should be given?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار MMR لأن high-dose systemic steroid يُعد severe immunosuppression عند الاستمرار عادةً ≥14 consecutive days في المرجع المقتبس، بينما الطفل أخذ 7 أيام فقط. كما أن التعرض كان قبل يومين، أي ضمن نافذة PEP باللقاح في الأشخاص المناسبين.
questions.reasoningEn: The source treats seven days of steroid exposure as insufficient to meet its severe-immunosuppression threshold and therefore selects MMR PEP.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Immunoglobulin يُستخدم في مجموعات high-risk أو عندما يكون live vaccine غير مناسب. No prophylaxis لا يطابق تعرض طفل غير محصن خلال نافذة PEP.
questions.clinicalPearl: For live-vaccine decisions, steroid dose and duration both matter.

tts.text: A 7-year-old unvaccinated child with asthma has been receiving methylprednisolone two milligrams per kilogram per day for seven days. He had contact with a measles case two days ago. What should be given? A. MMR vaccine. B. Immunoglobulin. C. No prophylaxis.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection 4th Ed 2026
sourceRefs.notes: Source cites Red Book 2024-2027 and an UpToDate steroid-immunosuppression threshold.

verification.referenceNotes: Time-sensitive PEP recommendation; current Red Book/CDC verification required.

questions.topic: Immunization, Infection Control, and Isolation Precautions
questions.stemEn: A medically healthy 4-month-old infant had contact with a measles case; the time since exposure is not stated. What should be given?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار immunoglobulin، لكن timing of exposure غير مذكور وهو عنصر أساسي في measles PEP. لذلك نسجل المفتاح كـrecall فقط ونضع السؤال للمراجعة.
questions.reasoningEn: The source answer is immune globulin for a four-month-old infant, but post-exposure timing is omitted.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: لا يمكن تثبيت بقية الخيارات دون معرفة نافذة التعرض والإرشاد الحالي للعمر.
questions.clinicalPearl: Measles PEP depends on age, immune status and time from exposure.

tts.text: A medically healthy four-month-old infant had contact with a measles case; the time since exposure is not stated. What should be given? A. MMR vaccine. B. Immunoglobulin. C. No prophylaxis.

questions.topic: Immunization, Infection Control, and Isolation Precautions
questions.stemEn: After exposure to varicella, which child is anticipated to have more severe infection?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يذكر long-term salicylate therapy ضمن الفئات ذات increased risk for moderate-to-severe varicella، لذلك الإجابة C.
questions.reasoningEn: Long-term salicylate therapy is listed by the source among higher-risk groups for clinically important varicella.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: العمر أقل من 12 سنة بحد ذاته ليس high-risk clue هنا، وotitis أوantibiotic use ليسا risk factors المعتمدة في المصدر.
questions.clinicalPearl: Risk stratification matters because prophylaxis and antiviral treatment decisions differ for high-risk patients.

tts.text: After exposure to varicella, which child is anticipated to have more severe infection? A. Age less than twelve years. B. Concurrent otitis media. C. Chronic salicylate treatment. D. Infection preceded by antibiotic use.

questions.topic: Immunization, Infection Control, and Isolation Precautions
questions.subtopic: Varicella post-exposure prophylaxis in immunocompromised child
questions.stemEn: A child with systemic lupus erythematosus on oral steroid 20 mg twice daily is exposed to varicella. What should be given?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار VZIG. لكن steroid dose relative to body weight وtiming from exposure غير مذكورين، وهما مهمان في PEP؛ لذا نحتاج current Red Book verification قبل اعتماد verifiedAnswer.
questions.reasoningEn: The source treats this steroid-treated SLE patient as high-risk and selects VZIG.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Live varicella vaccine قد يكون contraindicated في significant immunosuppression؛ الحاجة إلى acyclovir تعتمد على الإرشاد والسياق والتوقيت.
questions.clinicalPearl: Varicella PEP is highly dependent on immune status and timing.

tts.text: A child with systemic lupus erythematosus on oral steroid twenty milligrams twice daily is exposed to varicella. What should be given? A. Varicella-zoster immune globulin. B. Varicella-zoster immune globulin and acyclovir. C. Acyclovir alone. D. Varicella vaccine alone.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection 4th Ed 2026
sourceRefs.notes: Source cites Red Book management of varicella exposures.

questions.topic: Immunization, Infection Control, and Isolation Precautions
questions.stemEn: A child has hepatitis A. What should be given to his healthy 4-month-old brother after exposure?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار immunoglobulin للـ4-month-old exposed infant، لأن هذا العمر أصغر من العمر المعتاد للقاح Hepatitis A. التوقيت بعد exposure يجب أن يُراجع قبل النشر.
questions.reasoningEn: The recalled answer uses immune globulin for post-exposure prophylaxis in an infant too young for routine hepatitis A vaccination.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Hepatitis A vaccine ليس routine option في عمر 4 أشهر، وreassurance وحدها لا تقدم PEP.
questions.clinicalPearl: Hepatitis A PEP depends on age, timing and host risk factors.

tts.text: A child has hepatitis A. What should be given to his healthy four-month-old brother after exposure? A. Hepatitis A vaccine. B. Immunoglobulin. C. Reassurance.

questions.topic: Immunization, Infection Control, and Isolation Precautions
questions.stemEn: The family of a 12-year-old girl due to receive MMR and HPV vaccines is concerned about vaccine safety and adverse effects. What is the best way to address their concern?

options.text: Encourage them to talk with other parents
Give them scientific materials about vaccine safety
Tell them about consequences of not receiving vaccination

questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار B ويؤكد أن التواصل one-to-one مع pediatrician مطّلع ومهتم، مع توفير reputable vaccine-safety information، هو العامل الأهم في معالجة vaccine hesitancy. الخيارات لا تتضمن هذا الوصف الكامل، لذا B هو الأقرب.
questions.reasoningEn: The source emphasizes respectful, individualized clinician communication supported by reputable safety information.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Talking only to other parents قد يضيف misinformation. التخويف من consequences وحده أقل جودة من معالجة المخاوف مباشرة وبمعلومات موثوقة.
questions.clinicalPearl: Use a respectful, presumptive-but-open conversation and address the family’s specific concern with trusted evidence.

tts.text: The family of a twelve-year-old girl due to receive MMR and HPV vaccines is concerned about vaccine safety and adverse effects. What is the best way to address their concern? A. Encourage them to talk with other parents. B. Give them scientific materials about vaccine safety. C. Tell them about consequences of not receiving vaccination.
